title: Fly drumming: Red Happy's style and Moore's multiple sticks
summary: Moore explains foundation versus fly drummer, two-beat and four-beat playing, stick tricks, and how he uses four or even nine sticks and sits high.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So, back to Red Happy. What style of drumming would he use? Would he beat 4-4 or 2-4? Or both or what? He beat both. They used both, huh?

Both. And his show, show drumming, some drumming, type of the, uh, in some numbers called for, what they call, beat two. I mean, two beat. That mean the foundation, to hold a band together. Mm-hmm. In some numbers he beat four. But he was good on both of them. Mm-hmm. He was what you call a foundation drummer. And a fly drummer, too.
But what does a fly drummer do like him?

Well, a fly drummer takes solo, take a lot of tricks. Drums, solos, and cleave control. Throw the sticks up in the air. And Red Happy did all that? Yeah, throw the sticks up in the air and kept them all behind them. He was using around like four or five sticks. That's the apocondy line, he used four sticks. I use four sticks now. All at once? Yeah. What do you do? Well, I have, I have two on my arm. Mm-hmm.
And two on my hand. See?

If I have some sticks, I'll demonstrate it to you. Yeah, well, is it like juggling? Is that what it is? Something like juggling, but you're moving with rhythm. Mm-hmm. I mean, you can't, you know, I can't speak for that. You switch the sticks around. Yeah. Well, you take a stick from here and put it in your mouth. Yeah. You take a stick from here and put it in your mouth. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. You take a stick from here and put it in your mouth. Mm-hmm. See? You take it from here and put it in this arm. You're moving all the time. There's a picture. Yeah. Right in the rhythm. I used to use eight sticks. No, nine sticks I used to use. But I have to be sitting in a straight chair to use nine sticks. I put one on each side here I'm sitting on. I put a stick stand up if I can get to them. I have one between the legs and two on the bass drum. Mm-hmm. And still have me stick some arms. Oh, yeah. And I'm drumming still. I've got to use a space to put the other stick, the third stick all the time. It seems very complicated, but I used to use, I could use nine sticks better than I could four. I could balance myself better like that. But I can't sit on a drum stool. I have to sit on a regular square chair to do that. And I, since I've been, since I got a little bit ageable, I can't drum sitting down low. I have to sit up high, take that weight off my, to care for my leg. You sit down low, drum, any drummer sit down low. You can't, they can't keep them four beats up all the way through. They get tired in there, in the end step or even in the catheter's leg. You've got to sit up high and have some support up in here. You've got to stiffen the muscles in there for your four.
